items.prompt:
**Statement:** Notice in a housing society: 'Residents are requested to switch off the corridor lights after 11 p.m. to save electricity.'

**Assumptions:**
I. Switching off the corridor lights after 11 p.m. will save some electricity.
II. Residents do not use the corridors at all after 11 p.m.

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: the request is made "to save electricity", which only makes sense if switching off the lights saves some.
II is not implicit: the society only assumes the lights are not essential then; "do not use at all" is an extreme claim it need not believe.
Answer: Only assumption I is implicit.
solution.trap: An action taken for a purpose assumes the action serves that purpose — nothing more.

items.prompt:

**Assumptions:**

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: the advice is pointless unless that bus reaches before 9 o'clock.
II is implicit: advising her to take the bus assumes such a bus exists and is available to her.
Answer: Both I and II are implicit.
solution.trap: Advice assumes both that it is possible to follow and that following it works.

options: Only assumption I is implicit

Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is not implicit: calling it a "family pack" suggests who it suits, but the advertiser need not believe that only families will buy it.
II is not implicit: the advertisement makes no comparison with other brands.
Answer: Neither I nor II is implicit.
solution.trap: The advertiser assumes some buyers want a bigger pack — not "only families" and not "the best".

items.prompt:

**Assumptions:**

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is not implicit: the principal only needs to think the forecast is reliable enough to act on, not "always accurate".
II is implicit: closing the school because of the forecast assumes heavy rain would cause problems for students.
Answer: Only assumption II is implicit.
solution.trap: "Always" makes I far stronger than what the principal needs to believe.

items.prompt:

I. The shopkeeper may have the biscuits with the blue wrapper.

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: nobody asks a shopkeeper for an item he believes the shop cannot have.
II is not implicit: the son liking these biscuits does not mean he dislikes all others.
Answer: Only assumption I is implicit.
solution.trap: Liking one thing does not imply disliking everything else.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Anjali, who must reach the interview centre by 10 a.m., said: 'The only ways I can get there are the 8:30 bus and the 9 o'clock metro, and I am sure I will be on time.'

**Assumptions:**
I. The 8:30 bus will get Anjali to the centre by 10 a.m.
II. The 9 o'clock metro will get Anjali to the centre by 10 a.m.

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: Anjali need not assume I (she could plan on the metro) and need not assume II (she could plan on the bus), so neither is implicit on its own.
But since these are her only two ways and she is sure of being on time, she must assume that at least one of them gets her there by 10 a.m. So either I or II is implicit.
Answer: Either I or II is implicit.
solution.trap: Choosing "Both" assumes she relies on each route; her certainty needs only one of them to work.

items.prompt:

options: Only assumption I is implicit

Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is not implicit: the doctor's advice is about blood sugar and does not depend on the patient having no other problem.
II is implicit: the advice is given for blood-sugar control, so the doctor assumes walking helps.
Answer: Only assumption II is implicit.
solution.trap: I is beyond the scope of the advice.

items.prompt:

Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: a notice is put up only if the authority expects passengers to read it.
II is implicit: the advice would be pointless if unattended luggage faced no risk (of theft, loss or security checks).
Answer: Both I and II are implicit.
solution.trap: Every notice assumes it will be read; every warning assumes a risk exists.

items.prompt:

options: Only assumption I is implicit

Both I and II are implicit

II is implicit: an incentive is offered only if the company believes it can change behaviour.
Answer: Both I and II are implicit.
solution.trap: A remedy assumes both that the problem exists and that the remedy works.

items.prompt:

But he says a win needs at least one of the two and he is certain of winning, so he must assume at least one will happen: either I or II is implicit.

items.prompt:

items.prompt:

options: Only assumption I is implicit

Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is not implicit: a separate counter can be justified by their difficulty in standing in queues, not by how often they come.
II is implicit: a special counter would be pointless if no senior citizen ever came.
Answer: Only assumption II is implicit.
solution.trap: I invents a comparison; the board only assumes senior citizens will come.

Both I and II are implicit

Both I and II are implicit

Both I and II are implicit

Both I and II are implicit

items.prompt:

solution.trap: A planner never assumes the failure of his own plan.

items.prompt:

items.prompt:

Both I and II are implicit

items.prompt:

Both I and II are implicit

But the phone can come only from these two, and he promises it by Saturday, so he must assume at least one will deliver in time: either I or II is implicit.

solution.trap: His promise rests on one source succeeding, not both.

items.prompt:

items.prompt:

Both I and II are implicit

II is not implicit: if every student already met the condition, the rule would be pointless; the principal expects some may fall short.

items.prompt:

Both I and II are implicit

items.prompt:

Both I and II are implicit

solution.trap: II is hidden inside "the earlier you start, the more you will have" — the claim is false without returns.

**Statement:** The municipal commissioner said: 'We will impose a fine of ₹500 on anyone found throwing garbage on the streets.'

**Assumptions:**

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: a fine is imposed to deter; the commissioner assumes it will deter at least some people.
II is not implicit: if lack of dustbins were assumed to be the cause, a fine would not be the answer; the statement gives no cause.
Answer: Only assumption I is implicit.
solution.trap: A penalty assumes deterrence works, not any particular cause of the problem.

It has said that customers who visit a branch only for these services will be charged ₹20 per visit from next quarter.

**Assumptions:**
I. Most of the bank's customers do not know how to use a mobile app.

options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is not implicit: the plan relies on customers using the app; assuming most cannot would defeat it.
II is implicit: moving these services to the app can reduce crowding only if such visitors form a good part of the crowd.
Answer: Only assumption II is implicit.
solution.trap: The bank's remedy shows what it believes causes the crowding.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: The city police have announced that from 1 November, two-wheeler riders caught without a helmet will have their licence suspended for three months, instead of only paying a fine as at present.

**Assumptions:**
I. The present fine has had no effect at all on helmet use.
II. Most two-wheeler riders in the city do not wear helmets.

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is not implicit: the police only need to think the fine alone is not enough; "no effect at all" is extreme.
II is not implicit: a tougher penalty is justified even if a sizeable minority, not most, ride without helmets.
Answer: Neither I nor II is implicit.
solution.trap: Tightening a rule assumes the old one was insufficient, not useless, and not that most people break it.

**Assumptions:**
I. Being close to residential areas will help the firm deliver groceries faster.

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: the stores are placed in residential areas for the 20-minute target, so nearness is assumed to speed delivery.
II is not implicit: a firm may speed up delivery to win customers or beat rivals even if present customers are satisfied.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: The organising committee of a city marathon said: 'The race can be held on 12 January only if the police permit the closure of the main road or the Sports Authority lets us use the stadium loop, and we are confident the race will be held on 12 January.'

**Assumptions:**
I. The police will permit the closure of the main road.
II. The Sports Authority will let the committee use the stadium loop.

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: The committee need not assume I (the stadium loop could be the plan) or II (the main road could be the plan), so neither is implicit on its own.
But the race needs at least one of these, and the committee is confident it will be held, so it must assume at least one permission will come: either I or II is implicit.
Answer: Either I or II is implicit.
solution.trap: Confidence in the outcome needs just one route to succeed.

options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit

Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: the scholarship is the university's answer to falling numbers, so it assumes the money will attract some students.

**Statement:** News item: A state government has announced a 50 per cent cut in the road tax on electric cars for the next three years, saying that the high price of electric cars is the main reason people do not buy them.

**Assumptions:**

An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.

Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

steps: I is implicit: the cut is aimed at the price problem, so the government assumes road tax forms part of the cost of buying.
II is implicit: halving a tax that is already zero would mean nothing; the announcement assumes there is a tax to cut.
